content: Post-transplantation diabetes mellitus (PTDM) is a specific type of diabetes that develops after an organ transplantation procedure, regardless of the timing of its onset. This condition carries significant clinical implications for transplant recipients, as it is closely linked to an elevated risk of developing cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Hyperglycemia is a very common occurrence immediately following transplantation, with approximately 80% of kidney transplant recipients experiencing elevated blood glucose levels during the initial weeks post-surgery. This hyperglycemia is often attributed to stress-induced or steroid-related mechanisms. In many cases, this transient hyperglycemia resolves by the time the patient is discharged from the hospital.
